title: Trump Crypto Took $100 Million From a Businessman With Red Flags
partialText: The curious case of Guren “Bobby” Zhou shows the ease with which investors with shady backgrounds and unknown motivations can funnel money to the president.

title: The Lonely Crew at the Kennedy Center Will Miss Its…Mice
partialText: Employees say the performing arts center’s quirky-looking mice have an exotic back story. Do they?

title: Senate Bows to Reality, Leaving Trump’s Voting Bill Undone
partialText: The summer exit confirmed what had been apparent for weeks: that Republicans lacked the votes to pass the voting restrictions the president has made a top priority.

title: Israel Rejects Trump’s 15-Point Plan to Disarm Hamas
partialText: President Trump’s Board of Peace announced an agreement last month that aimed at Hamas’s giving up its weapons alongside an Israeli withdrawal from Gaza.

title: Iran, Holding Firm to Hormuz, Pushes for Return to June MOU
partialText: The Strait of Hormuz is Iran’s best leverage to get Washington to release Iran’s frozen assets, lift economic sanctions and end its naval blockade.

title: Inside the War on Hezbollah’s Finances
partialText: Israel and the United States aren’t just targeting the Lebanese militant group’s weapons. They’re going after its money.

title: The U.S. Is Burning Through Weapons in Iran. Russia and China Are Taking Note.
partialText: The Iran war has depleted U.S. weapons stockpiles, resulting in a significant erosion of firepower. A more drawn-out Iran conflict benefits Moscow and Beijing, some analysts say.

title: Obama and Abdul El-Sayed Spoke to Discuss Unity After Michigan Senate Primary
partialText: Dr. Abdul El-Sayed’s call with the former president comes as he tries to win over wary Democrats in Michigan’s high-stakes Senate race.

title: Michigan Senate Candidate, a Former Trump Critic, Shifts Toward Election Skepticism
partialText: Mike Rogers, the Republican nominee, has suggested that further scrutiny of the 2020 election was warranted and that voting irregularities sank his first Senate bid two years ago.

title: Poll: Voters See Political Parties as More Extreme Than Their Own Candidates
partialText: In a New York Times/Siena poll of battleground states, national parties were seen as too far to the right or the left, while nominees were viewed as more moderate.

title: How a Drone ‘Hellscape’ Might Stop a Chinese Invasion of Taiwan
partialText: Inspired by Ukraine’s battlefield gains, Taiwan is betting on drones to deter a potential Chinese invasion.

title: The ‘Furthur’ Bus’s Long, Strange Trip, and Why It’s Returning to San Francisco
partialText: The psychedelic bus whose passengers hit the road and fueled ’60s counterculture is coming back out. And to its owners, America sure could use it.

title: Anthony Scaramucci, Podcast Star, Explains U.S. Politics to the World
partialText: He spent 11 days in the Trump White House nine years ago. Now he has a hit podcast, helping the British public, among others, understand what’s going on.

title: BTS’s Grammys Boycott Highlights the Perils of Pop Music
partialText: The genre was shaped by exclusion, not expansion.

title: A Generation on Antidepressants Searches for the Exit
partialText: Many people feel that antidepressants block their true emotions, but they don’t have guidance about how to get off these drugs.

title: The Pope’s Favorite Team
partialText: Are the Chicago White Sox blessed?

title: Hunter Biden Says His Father’s Cancer Is Worsening
partialText: In an interview with the BBC, Mr. Biden said that former President Joseph R. ⁠Biden Jr.’s prostate cancer had spread into his bones and was causing pain.
